_doc: Committed mutation-survivor ratchet for the weekly `mutants` workflow (.github/workflows/mutants.yml, ADR-0031). Each key below is a crate whose surviving-mutant count is FROZEN at `max_survivors`: the sweep fails and opens a tracking issue when `just mutants -p <crate>` reports MORE survivors than the committed number — i.e. a test that used to catch a mutant no longer does. A crate ABSENT from this file is swept report-only (never red) until it is reinforced and given an entry, mirroring ADR-0031's per-crate 'advisory, then blocking once the baseline is clean'. Lower an entry as survivors are killed to tighten the ratchet; never raise one to hide a real regression. POST-COLLAPSE (v0.5 18->3): the former building-block crates were folded into `aozora` and the LSP into `aozora-cli`; both are temporarily absent here (report-only) until a fresh mutation sweep of the merged surface commits new numbers. `aozora-ffi` / `aozora-extism` are unchanged and stay armed.

aozora-ffi.reason: Clean after reinforcement (5 killable survivors killed, host lane: 5 -> 0 missed). All 5 were `delete -` on the `AozoraStatus` discriminants (`NullInput = -1` through `SourceTooLarge = -5`): every behavioural test compared a returned code against `AozoraStatus::Variant as c_int`, so flipping a discriminant moved the function's return value and the expected value together and the equality still held. A `status_discriminants_are_abi_stable` test now pins each variant to its literal wire integer (0, -1, -2, -3, -4, -5), which a sign flip breaks — killing all 5. Genuine gaps, not equivalents: the codes are a C ABI stability contract that embedders hard-code. The 1 unviable mutant (`into_owned_bytes -> Default::default()`) does not compile — `AozoraBytes` holds raw pointers and derives no `Default`. See #485.

aozora-extism.reason: Clean: the host-testable `logic` module has 0 missed over its 17 viable mutants, and the `wasm32`-only `plugin` module is excluded. `logic` (`guard_len` boundary, the six `render_*` serializers, `schema_version`) is fully pinned by the existing tests asserting every output is byte-identical to the shared `aozora::json` authority. The seven thin `#[plugin_fn]` wrappers in `mod plugin` are `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]`, so on a host sweep they are cfg-dead and every one of their ~49 mutants is a vacuous survivor; the module is isolated in `plugin.rs` and excluded via `mutants.toml` `exclude_globs` so the ratchet counts only real product surface. The 1 unviable mutant does not compile. See #485.
